newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard warns of Australian tax reform surprises.
newsitem.headline: Howard warns of Australian tax reform surprises.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, who has repeatedly rejected calls for tax reform before the next election, said on Wednesday that voters should watch out for surprises in that area.

"You can always rely on one thing about me and that is that in the course of being in government there will always be a few surprises," Howard told Sydney radio station 2UE on the morning after the release of the budget for the year to June 30, 1998.
Howard had been asked when progress could be expected on tax reform.
Earlier in the interview, Howard described the government's achievement in turning a budget deficit of A$10 billion into a A$1.6 billion surplus in 1998/99 as "colossal."
He said the budget created the conditions for growth, because it would reduce debt.
"By getting rid of debt, we are laying the foundation for solid growth," Howard said.
He made no comment on interest rates.

Howard said the budget did not include any estimate of how much the government would have to pay in compensation to aboriginal groups because of the government's decisions on the Wik native title case.

He said it was too early to know how much the government would have to pay. The government has said it would pay 75 percent of any compensation payouts to aboriginal groups who are affected by the changes.
"It's very, very difficult to determine what the final outcome will be and in any event it will be some time in the future," he said.
